probeMissions: M1 `m1-ladder` — the whole ladder as an operator would plainly write it. Copy examples/request-triage to a temp root; add src/guard.ts, src/lib/deep/guard.ts and src/cafe\u0301.ts (NFD on disk), each exporting assertGrounded; rewrite the Evidence cell of the eight `applied` rows of runward/floor.md with, in order: file:src/guard.ts#assertGrounded (exact), file:src/Guard.TS (wrong case in the FILE component), file:SRC/guard.ts (wrong case in a DIRECTORY component), file:src/LIB/deep/guard.ts (wrong case in a nested directory), file:src/nope.ts (does not exist), file:../outside.ts (escapes upward), file:src/caf\u00e9.ts (typed NFC, spelled NFD on disk); the remaining rows become `n/a` with a reason. Baseline `check --strict --json`: exit 1, 6 conformance gaps, three of them the spelling message. RESULT: 0/15 mutants observable — every case divergence here is re-derived by spellingViaRealpath.

M2 `m2-unmasked` — the same divergences written with a redundant `./` segment (file:./src/Guard.TS, file:./SRC/guard.ts, file:./src/LIB/deep/guard.ts, file:./SRC/lib/DEEP/guard.ts, file:./src/caf\u00e9.ts) plus one exact row. Baseline: exit 1, 5 conformance gaps, all five the spelling message. RESULT: 3/15 observable (the three L274 rungs), 5 gaps -> 1.

M3 `m3-exact` — every pointer spelled exactly as the disk spells it, in all four forms (plain, nested, `./`, NFD). Baseline: exit 0, verdict clean, 0 conformance gaps. The false-RED detector: a guard that refuses everything would satisfy the other missions. RESULT: 0/15 observable — no mutant invents a spelling violation.

M4 `m4-unreadable` — a directory the walk can traverse but not list. Same base mission plus `locked/guard.ts`, then `chmod 111 locked`, so readdirSync throws EACCES while existsSync/statSync/realpath/readFile all still work. Rows: file:locked/guard.ts (exact), file:locked/Guard.TS (wrong case, still caught by the realpath fallback), file:./locked/Guard.TS (wrong case, unmasked, and reported by nothing today). Baseline: exit 1, 1 conformance gap. This is the only way into the `catch`. RESULT: 1/15 observable (the empty catch).

M5 `m5-repo` — the repository fallback of resolvePointer (evidence.ts:316), which calls onDiskSpelling with no realpath fallback. Layout: <repo>/.git (marker), <repo>/shared/{guard.ts,lib/deep/guard.ts,cafe\u0301.ts}, and the mission at <repo>/proj (a copy of examples/request-triage). Rows point out of the three bases but stay inside the repo: file:../shared/Guard.TS, file:../SHARED/guard.ts, file:../SHARED/lib/DEEP/guard.ts, file:../shared/caf\u00e9.ts, plus one exact row. Baseline: exit 1, 4 conformance gaps. RESULT: 3/15 observable (the three L274 rungs).

M6 `m6-case-only` — M2 with the Unicode row removed, so the ONLY defect in the mission is case divergence. Baseline: exit 1, verdict `gaps`, 4 conformance gaps. This is the false-GREEN detector and it is where the headline evidence comes from. RESULT: 3/15 observable, each as an EXIT CODE flip 1 -> 0.

M7 `m7-repo` — M5 with the Unicode row removed: the same false-green detector on the resolvePointer branch that has no fallback behind it. Baseline: exit 1, 3 conformance gaps. RESULT: 3/15 observable, each as an exit code flip 1 -> 0.

Plus a sweep against runward's own mission: 0/15 observable, as expected — no pointer in this repository has a diverging spelling, so the self-gate cannot exercise this function whatever the probe does. Eight ledgers, 120 measurements, at reports/mutation/probe-{selfgate,m1..m7}.jsonl in the probe worktree, all written by the corrected scripts/mutation-probe.mjs.

Builder (rebuilds all seven from scratch): scratchpad/build-missions.mjs; clean-tree baseline reader: scratchpad/baselines.mjs; single-mutant observer: scratchpad/observe.mjs; whole-net runner: scratchpad/net.mjs. All four use `check --strict --json`.
base: init --yes --example, green. Every other mission is a copy carrying exactly one deliberate change, and the pristine verdict of each was read BEFORE any mutant was applied.

m-crow-green: a self-citation, plus one line above the heading with a LEADING pipe, NO trailing pipe, and a first cell carrying whitespace. Pristine exit 1, one gap. The shape that separates startsWith from endsWith.
m-crow-red: the same self-citation, and above the heading an honest sentence that merely ENDS with a pipe. Pristine exit 0, clean.
m-crow-prose and m-crow-bare: pipe-free prose, and nothing at all. The controls for the pipe-free region and for the must-stay-red case.

m-spell and m-spell-dir: one pointer mis-cased on its file, and on a DIRECTORY segment, nothing else changed, so the divergence is the ONLY violation. Pristine exit 1 with exactly one gap. m-spell-control: untouched, carried through every capture so 'this mission did not move' is distinguishable from 'nothing moves'.

conformanceRow BATTERY, 4591 markdown blocks read through evidenceReport itself using the unit test's own oracle: 0 problems means the block was KEPT, 1 means the function called it a row. Leads times first cells times separators times statuses times tails; the same shapes behind three fence styles; 237 pipe-free shapes including five pipe LOOK-ALIKE characters, NBSP, U+2028, BOM, 4000-character lines and mixed blocks; plus all 23 cases the unit test pins, asserted to read as that test pins them.
conformanceRow FUZZ, 6000 blocks from a seeded xorshift32 so it is a fixture and not a lottery, 4000 of them guaranteed pipe-free — density in the one region the two guard mutants can act in.

onDiskSpelling DIRECT BATTERY, 329 calls on a purpose-built fixture: mixed-case directories and files, the five Unicode fold rungs, an NFD-named file, a ten-deep path, an empty directory and a 0111 directory. Each target fed in seven shapes — plain, one/two/three trailing separators, a doubled inner separator, an extra leading separator, every segment doubled — plus 14 absolute edge cases. Paths concatenated BY HAND, not with path.join, because join() normalises away exactly the shapes the loop bound is about.

CASE-SENSITIVE REPRODUCTION: a 300 MB case-sensitive APFS sparse image, verified case-sensitive by probe. Every mission copied onto it and re-measured, and the whole unit net re-run with TMPDIR pointing into it, so 'survives on ubuntu-latest' is MEASURED here rather than inferred from process.platform. The volume was probed for normalisation too: a file written NFC is found under its NFD name, so it is case-sensitive but normalisation-insensitive, and that limit is stated wherever it matters.

verdicts.evidence: Ran scripts/mutation-probe.mjs (corrected, --strict) on all seven missions plus the self-gate: identical `check --strict --json` payload every time (8/8 'no observable difference'). Ran the whole net (unit suite, smoke, OSCAL, in-toto, audit corpus, self-gate --strict) with the sibling mutant at the same line applied: all six legs exit 0. COULD NOT CLEAR. This mutant forces `cur = sep` unconditionally, which is a no-op only while `parts[0] === ""` — true for every path this function receives on POSIX, and measured rather than read: onDiskSpelling is only ever called with a `path.resolve()` result, and `path.posix.resolve` yields an empty component at index 0 and nowhere else ('/a/b'.split('/') -> ['','a','b']; resolve('//x/y','z').split('/') -> ['','x','y','z'], the '//' collapsed). On win32 the same measurement gives win32.resolve('C:\\proj','src\\a.ts').split('\\') -> ['C:','proj','src','a.ts'], so the mutant would set cur to '\\' instead of 'C:\\' — a drive-RELATIVE walk, which is verbatim the defect the first windows-latest CI leg found on 2026-08-17 and which this line exists to fix. I have no Windows runner here and the suite has no win32 fixture, so nothing in runward's net can distinguish this mutant on any platform. Filed as a hole per the rule that an undecidable mutant is over-reported, not cleared. The work it names is shared with the four mutants below: make the drive-root computation reachable by a test (extract it as an exported pure function taking a path flavour, or add a win32-only fixture that plants a mis-spelled pointer).

verdicts.evidence: The extra iteration runs and does nothing, and the battery was proven able to SEE an extra iteration before that was believed. Direct drive, 329 calls: pristine 117 verified / 182 path / 14 unreadable / 16 null, digest 894c010b; mutant the same four counts and the same digest, 0 of 329 differ, second pristine run identical. FIXTURE ASSERTED, not assumed: 43 of the 45 plain-shape cases answer non-null, exact spellings answer verified, all five fold rungs answer with the on-disk name, the unlistable directory answers unreadable. A FIRST VERSION of this battery built its paths with path.join and silently produced 268 nulls out of 329 — paths that did not exist — which would have read as a beautiful equivalence; that fixture defect was found and corrected before any reading was believed. SENSITIVITY CONTROLS, all in this function, none on any list: narrowing the bound by one moves 117 of 329 and flips a mission; starting the walk at 2 moves 183; removing the empty-segment guard moves 236. THE DECISIVE ONE: removing that guard AND widening the bound exactly as this mutant widens it changes a further 65 answers and THROWS on 10 of them — so the iteration at the end IS genuinely executed and genuinely observable, and the reason this mutant is invisible is that the empty-segment guard absorbs the undefined segment before anything else in the loop body runs. Not a blind instrument: an absorbed difference.

verdicts.evidence: Identical `check --strict --json` payload on all seven probe missions and the self-gate (8/8 'no observable difference'). COULD NOT CLEAR. Removing the `!want` skip only matters when a path component is empty. Measured, not read: onDiskSpelling only ever receives a `path.resolve()` result, `path.posix.resolve` collapses '//' (resolve('//x/y','z').split('/') -> ['','x','y','z']) and produces an empty component at index 0 only, while the loop starts at index 1 — so on this platform the guard never fires and no mission can reach it. The one shape that does reach it is a Windows UNC or extended-length path: win32.resolve('\\\\server\\share','x\\y').split('\\') -> ['','','server','share','x','y'] and '\\\\?\\C:\\proj' -> ['','','?','C:',...], both with an empty component at index 1. I cannot run either here, and the suite has no win32 fixture, so nothing in runward's net distinguishes this mutant on any platform. Filed as a hole rather than argued equivalent, per the rule that an undecidable mutant is over-reported. It shares the remedy of the five drive-root mutants above: one exported, path-flavour-parameterised walk that a unit test can feed win32-shaped input to.
